**Start (seam with B).** I read line 112.5 (n113) as: `ཡིད་དྲན་པར་གྱིས་ཤིག༔ ཀྱཻ་རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ རང་གི་ད་ལྟ་ངོ་མ་ཤེས་ནས་སྐྲག་ན༔ ཞི་བའི་སྐུ་ཐམས་ཅད་མགོན་པོ་ནག་པོའི་སྐུ་རུ་འཆར་རོ༔`. It ends in `༔` against the right frame.
- p. 113 opens, after the ornament, with `ཁྲོ་བོའི་སྐུ་ཐམས་ཅད…`. The seam is clean and needs no fix. The first word of 112.5 (`ཡིད`) belongs to B's 112.4/5 join; B should confirm it.

**END: I propose ending at 115.5 after `…ཡི་དམ་རིན་པོ་ཆེ་ཞེས་བོས་ལ་གསོལ་བ་ཐོབ་ཅིག༔`.** That is the `༔` at about x≈1470 of the straightened n116 line 5, just before the line's last words, `ཁྱོད་རང་གི་བླ་མའི་`.
- This closes the call on the yidam (115.2–115.5: "if you recognise them they are yidam deities … remember the Three Jewels, remember your yidam, call it by name … call 'Precious yidam!' and pray"). The next sentence turns to the lama.

- Under this proposal, part 013 starts mid-line 115.5 with `ཁྱོད་རང་གི་བླ་མའི་` and then 116.1. I transcribed all of 115.5 in read_C.txt so that the editor can split the line.
- **Fallback (to end with the lama call as well):** finish on 116.1 at `…ཐུགས་རྗེས་མ་བཏང་བར་གྱིས་ལ་གསོལ་བ་ཐོབ་ཅིག༔`, just before `ཁྲག…`, at about x≈1800, near the end of the line. I read 116.1 at ×3 only, as `མཚན་ནས་བརྗོད་ལ༔ བདག་བར་དོར་འཁྱམས་ནས་ཡོད་པས་ར་མདའ་མཛོད་ཅིག༔ ཐུགས་རྗེས་མ་བཏང་བར་གྱིས་ལ་གསོལ་བ་ཐོབ་ཅིག༔ ཁྲག…`. Part 013's reader should re-read it.

**Proposed `# name:`** `The rest of the Īśvarīs and the Lord of Death`. Alternatives: `Yama, Lord of Death, and the call to the yidam`; `Day twelve ends: the Lord of Death`.
- pp. 107.3–115.5 cover the twenty-eight Īśvarīs from the south onward and the summing-up after them (107–112, from A/B's pages, which I have not read). Then come the Lord of Death (Yama) appearing to one who fails to recognise (112.5–114.1), the teaching that he is empty display (114.2–115.2), and the call on the yidam (115.2–5).

## Method

- Skew found per image by maximising row-profile variance; all reading done on rotated copies.
- Line bands from the row profile. Each line was cropped in four overlapping segments at ×3 (LANCZOS).
- Doubtful syllables were enlarged ×6–×10, some binarised and enlarged NEAREST. I also made side-by-side montages, for example `ཡོང` at 113.5 against `ཡོད` at 113.5 and `ཡིད` at 113.2.
- The other recension (witness_ga.txt) was used only to know which words to expect.

| place | as written | candidates / why |
|---|---|---|
| 113.4 | `ནམ་མཁའ[?]་དང་མཉམ་པ` | The second stack is མཁ followed by a letter like འ/ར that is fused to the next stack. There is no `འི` and no `མཐའ`. The other recension has `ནམ་མཁའི་མཐའ་དང་མཉམ་པ`. `མཁའ` is the only word that fits. |
| 113.5 | `ཡོང[?]་ངོ༔` | The first letter against the frame has three prongs and a left-hand hook. It is like the ཡ of `ཡོད` (113.5) but blurred, and འ is possible. The other recension has `འོང་ངོ`, and this print has `ཡོང་ངོ` at 114.2. Either way the sense is the same. |
| 114.1 | `ཀླད་པ་འཐུང[?]་བ༔` | Between `པ` and `བ`, at ×8, I see a box-like letter with an open top-left (འ), a ཐ-like stack with a ུ, and ང. The tshegs are fused. The other recension has `ཀླད་པ་འཐུང་བ`. |
| 114.2 | `སྐྲག་པར[?]་མ་བྱེད་ཅིག༔` | I count four stacks between `སྐྲ` and `བྱེ` (ག, a narrow པ, a ར-like stack, མ), so I take `པར`. The other recension has `སྐྲག་པ་མ་བྱེད`. The sense is the same. |
| 114.3 | `སྟོང་ཉིད་རང་གཟུགས[?]` | `གཟུགས` is cramped. The other recension has `སྟོང་པའི་རང་གཟུགས`, but this print clearly has `ཉིད`. |

| 115.4 | `མཚན་ནས་གང་ཐོན[?]་བོས་ཅིག༔` | The stacks are ག, ང, then ཐ (or ཕ) with an o-sign, ན, བ with an o-sign, ས, then `ཅིག`. I read `གང་ཐོན` as "whatever [name] comes up", which is unusual. The other recension has only `མཚན་ནས་བོས་ཤིག`. |

## Where the print differs from the other recension (print followed)

Spelling only (same sense):
- 113.2 `བསྐལ་བར`; 113.4 `འབྲིང་པོ་ནི` for `འབྲིང་བ་ནི`.
- 113.5 `ཡོང་ངོ` and 114.2 `ཡོང་ངོ`, for `འོང་ངོ`.
- 113.5 `མིག་ཏུ` for `མིག་དུ`; `བཅིངས་པ` for `བཅིང་བ`.
- 114.3 `བཏུབས་པ` for `གཏུབ་པ`.
- 115.5 `བཟུང་ཞིག` for `ཟུངས་ཤིག`.
- `ཀྱཻ` (double e-sign) as usual, at 113.1 and 114.2.

Sense differences:
- **113.1** `…སྐུ་རུ་ཤར་ནས༔ རང་སྣང་བདུད་དུ་སོང་ནས…`: one sentence. The other recension has `…སྐུ་རུ་ཤར་ནས་རང་སྣང…`. The sense is the same.
- **113.3** **`རང་སྣང་དུ་ངོ་ཤེས་ན་ཤི་མ་ཐག་ཏུ…གཤིན་རྗེ…སྐུ་འཆར་རོ`** ("if you recognise [it] as self-appearance, Yama appears"). The other recension has `རང་སྣང་ངོ་མ་ཤེས་ན` ("if you do not recognise"). The context calls for the negative (see Suspected misprints). The print also adds `ཀྱི` in `ཆོས་ཉིད་ཀྱི་བར་དོར`.
- **113.4** `ནམ་མཁའ་དང་མཉམ་པ` ("equal to the sky"), without `མཐའ` ("the limit of the sky").
- **114.1** `ཁམས་ཐམས་ཅད་ཁེངས་ནས་ཡོང་ངོ` ("he comes filling all the world-realms"). The other recension has `ཁམས་གང་ནས་འོང་ངོ`.
- **114.3** `ཞེད་མི་དགོས་སོ` ("no need to fear"). The other recension has `བྲེད་སྔངས་མི་དགོས`. The letter is a rounded ཞ with an e-sign, not བྲ.
- **114.3** `སྟོང་ཉིད་རང་གཟུགས`, where the other recension has `སྟོང་པའི་རང་གཟུགས`.
- **114.4** `སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཀྱིས་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ལ་གླགས་མི་རྙེད`. The agent and the object are reversed (other recension: `སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ལ་སྟོང་ཉིད་ཀྱིས`). The meaning is close.
- **114.5** `མ་གཏོགས༔ ཕྱི་རོལ་དུ` for `མ་གཏོགས་པ༔ ཕྱི་རོལ་ན`.
- **115.1** `ལ་སོགས་དངོས་སུ` (no `པ༔`). **`དེ་ལྟར་ཐག་ཆོད་ན`** ("if you are thus decided"). The other recension has `དེ་ལྟར་ཤེས་ན`.
- **115.2** **`དེ་ལྟར་ངོ་ཤེས་ན་ནི་ཡི་དམ་གྱི་ལྷ་ཡིན་ནོ`** ("if you recognise them thus, they are yidam deities"). The other recension has `དེ་ལྟར་མ་ཤེས་ནའང` ("even if you do not recognise"). ངོ is clear at ×7, and there is no མ. The sentence makes sense as it stands, so it is kept.
- **115.3** `སྐྱབས་སུ་མཆིའོ་སྙམ་པའི` (no `༔` after `མཆིའོ`).
- **115.4** `ཁྱོད་རང་གི་ཡི་དམ་གང་ཡིན་པ`, without `གྱི་ལྷ`. **`མཚན་ནས་གང་ཐོན[?]་བོས་ཅིག`**, where the other recension has `མཚན་ནས་བོས་ཤིག`.
- **115.5** **`ར་མདའ་ལ་རྒྱུག་ཅིག`** ("run to [my] aid"; `རྒྱུ` with a long tail, then ག, clear at ×5). The other recension has `ར་མདའ་མཛོད་ཅིག`, and so does this print at 116.1 for the lama.
- **116.1** (fallback zone) `ཐུགས་རྗེས་མ་བཏང་བར་གྱིས་ལ`. The other recension has `ཐུགས་རྗེས་མ་གཏང་གྱིས་ལ`.

```
# fix: འཁྱམ་མོ༔ ཀྱཻརིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ རང་སྣང => འཁྱམ་མོ༔ ཀྱཻ་རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ རང་སྣང
# fix: རང་སྣང་ངོ་ཤེསན་གནད => རང་སྣང་ངོ་ཤེས་ན་གནད
# fix: རྒྱལ་པོའིསྐུ་འཆར => རྒྱལ་པོའི་སྐུ་འཆར
```

- There are no `པའཾ`, `ལཾ`, `ནམཁའ`, subscript-ས or -གས ligature forms on these pages.
- The 112.5/113.1 seam needs no fix. The 115.5/116.1 join (`བླ་མའི་|མཚན`) has a tsheg and needs none.

## Suspected misprints

1. **113.3 `རང་སྣང་དུ་ངོ་ཤེས་ན` → `རང་སྣང་དུ་ངོ་མ་ཤེས་ན`.** The image clearly shows `དུ` (ད with a ུ loop), then `ངོ`, then `ཤེས`, with no མ (×7). The sentence before says that recognising brings buddhahood "by one point, one word". This sentence then says Yama appears immediately after death, which only fits failing to recognise, and the other recension has `ངོ་མ་ཤེས་ན`. Certainty: moderate to high. Proposed: `# fix: རང་སྣང་དུ་ངོ་ཤེས་ན་ཤི => རང་སྣང་དུ་ངོ་མ་ཤེས་ན་ཤི` (rule 5b; the note gives the print's reading). If the editor prefers not to insert a syllable, keep it with a note.
2. **114.4 `དངོས[?]་པ་ཅན་དུ`** for `དངོས་པོ་ཅན་དུ` ("substantial"). The o-sign is missing on `པ`, and the first letter is doubtful. Only `དངོས་པོ་ཅན` makes sense. Certainty: moderate. Proposed: `# fix: དངོས་པ་ཅན་དུ => དངོས་པོ་ཅན་དུ`. Alternatively keep it, note only, if the editor counts `དངོས་པ` as the print's own spelling.
3. **115.2 `དེ་ལྟར་ངོ་ཤེས་ན་ནི`** (the other recension has `མ་ཤེས་ནའང`). It reads acceptably, so it is kept, note only.

## Open

- The end decision is for the editor: 115.5 after `…གསོལ་བ་ཐོབ་ཅིག༔` (proposed), or 116.1 after the parallel call on the lama (fallback).
- 116.1 was read at ×3 only; part 013's reader should confirm it.
